Install optional tools for tidygenclust

Source: R/tgc_tools_install.R
tgc_tools_install.Rd

The core functionality of tidygenclust is native: gt_radmix() and gt_clumppling() need neither Python nor conda. A few additional features rely on external tools, which are optional and are only installed on request:

  • fastmixture, a python package used by gt_fastmixture();

  • ADMIXTURE, used by tidypopgen::gt_admixture();

  • ADAMIXTURE, a python package used by gt_adamixture().

Usage

tgc_tools_install(
  tools = c("fastmixture", "admixture", "adamixture"),
  reset = FALSE,
  fastmixture_hash = "1f03a8980be4872341e5faca9d6f2dfc7ccbfe35",
  adamixture_version = "1.8.9",
  conda_yaml = "auto",
  ci_install = FALSE
)

Arguments

tools

a vector with the tools to install, any of "fastmixture", "admixture" and "adamixture". Defaults to all of them.

reset

a boolean used to reset the virtual environment. Only set to TRUE if you have a broken virtual environment that you want to reset.

fastmixture_hash

a string with the commit hash of the fastmixture version to install. Default is the latest tested version.

adamixture_version

a string with the version of ADAMIXTURE to install from PyPI. Default is the latest tested version.

conda_yaml

A vector of string with the path for the yaml files used for installation (one for ctidygenclust and, for osx only, one for admixture in x86 compatibility mode). The value of each string can either be "auto" (the default, select the latest available yaml that has been tested to work on a given operating system), NULL (let conda attempt to install the latest available packages from the internet), or a path to a specific conda yaml found in "inst/env_snapshots". For "auto" or NULL, it is also possible to provide a vector of length one, and the value will apply to all the conda environments (e.g. conda_yaml="auto" is equivalent to conda_yaml = c("auto", "auto") in osx); a single path is used for ctidygenclust (and "auto" for the environment of ADMIXTURE on osx). Tools that are not in tools are left out of the yaml files, as is fastmixture, which is always installed from github.

ci_install

a boolean indicating if the installation is being run on continuous integration (CI) services. Default is FALSE. If TRUE, the function will look for the conda yaml file in the inst/env_snapshots folder of the package source directory, rather than in the installed package directory. This is useful when testing the package on CI services.

Value

NULL (invisibly)

Details

We use reticulate to install them in a conda environment, ctidygenclust.

The optional tools are only available on Linux at the moment. On Windows, they can be used through the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). On macOS, the OpenMP library of the python tools conflicts with the one used by R packages such as bigstatsr, which crashes the R session.

tgc_tools_install() creates the conda environment with the chosen tools. If the environment already exists, it only adds the tools that are not installed yet (alternatively, use tgc_fastmixture_install(), tgc_admixture_install() and tgc_adamixture_install() to add a tool to an existing environment). tgc_tools_version() reports the tools that are installed.

For each tool, default to the latest version of these packages that has been tested to work with tidygenclust. It is possible to provide a more recent github commit for a specific tool, but this might lead to incompatibilities and errors.

The conda environment is created from a conda yaml file with the versions of all the packages that have been tested on each operating system (see conda_yaml); fastmixture is then installed from its github repository, and ADAMIXTURE from PyPI, with pip, run in the environment with reticulate::conda_run2(). If the installation fails with the tested yaml, you can try conda_yaml = NULL to let conda install the latest available packages.
